podcast.body: Ray Charles's early R&B classic, a song that was later famously sampled in a "chopped-up" form to form the basis of Kanye West's 2005 number one smash "Gold Digger." "Ray Charles's early R&B classic, I Got A Woman."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.body: This groundbreaking record, widely credited as the first soul record, was released as rock and roll and became Charles's first number one hit on the R&B chart. It was a new fusion of gospel, blues, big band jazz, and early rock and roll, utterly unlike anything recorded before, based on blues lyrics written by his trumpet player Renald Richard and set to a gospel tune by The Southern Tones. The song caused real problems with the gospel community, who viewed it as debasing something holy by using sacred musical styles for secular purposes, but it quickly became a rock and roll standard, covered by Elvis Presley, The Everly Brothers, The Beatles, and The Monkees. "I got a woman went to number one on the R&B chart and quickly entered the stage repertoire of another musician who had church music in his veins."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
